name: thank_you_card_payments
description: A payment request between 'amount entered' and 'money booked'. It exists so the PIN is one way to confirm a payment and a later tap on the payer's own device can be another, without touching the booking path again.

columns.name: card_id
columns.description: Whose money is being asked for — the card's owner pays.

columns.name: valid_until
columns.description: A request that is past this is not payable, whatever its state says.

notes: state is set to consumed BEFORE the booking runs. The consuming update is conditional on the row still being open, which is what makes it the lock: a second caller finds nothing to consume. A crash between the two steps therefore leaves 'request used, no money moved' rather than 'money moved, request still open' — and only the second of those can be booked twice.
Expiry is derived from valid_until on read, not written by a timer. An implementation that only looks at state will honour a request that expired an hour ago.
A consumed row is kept. It is what an old receipt refers to, together with the card row that must never be deleted.

The memo limit is the card's own constant, which happens to equal MEMO_MAX_CHARS. They are written separately because they are separate decisions — the column is varchar(512) and an unchecked longer memo comes back as a raw driver error.
Timestamps are UTC milliseconds; see types/Timestamp.json.
